## Tests

- [ ] T1. `roadmap/tests/test_validate_spike.py` accepts the new SpikeDefinition; `events/tests/test_envelope_schema.py` accepts the new example envelopes and still rejects every `events/examples/invalid/` file.
- [ ] T2. `events/subscribe` rejects a repository outside the caller's authorization, unknown filter keys, an HTTP callback, a redirecting callback and a private-address callback; a wrong challenge echo leaves the subscription inactive.
- [ ] T3. `events/unsubscribe` and expiry delete the subscription row and the Vault secret; later events are not POSTed.
- [ ] T4. Standard Webhooks signature produced by the relay verifies with the subscription secret and fails with any other secret.
- [ ] T5. The same envelope `id` delivered twice to the relay results in one POST; redelivery after a failed POST carries `attempt > 1`.
- [ ] T6. Suppression: bot author, draft PR, non-allowlisted repository and 5 `synchronize` events within 60 s produce 0, 0, 0 and 1 POST respectively, each with an audit reason.
- [ ] T7. The payload contains only envelope reference fields plus the generated summary; a fixture with a PR title/body in the source webhook never shows it in the POST body; the body is at most 256 KiB.
- [ ] T8. Callback 5xx/timeout triggers bounded backoff; the entry stays pending (no `XACK`) and succeeds on recovery; the relay restart test resumes from the pending list.
- [ ] T9. Static/grep check: the relay and subscription code contains no timer- or cron-driven GitHub or ChatGPT reads.

## Rollback

- Spike documents (tasks 1, 2, 8, 10) are plain files: revert the PR in `mctlhq/.github`.
- Proof code ships behind `MCTL_EVENTS_CHATGPT_RELAY_ENABLED` (default false). To roll back, set it to false, which stops the relay and removes `events` from advertised capabilities. Then delete the `chatgpt-relay` consumer group (`XGROUP DESTROY mctl:events:github chatgpt-relay`), the Valkey ACL user, stored subscriptions and their Vault secrets. Finally, remove the subscription/plugin connection in ChatGPT.
- The producer, the `mctl:events:github` stream and the `claude-remote` consumer group are never changed, and `codex-watch` and Telegram/Slack notifications are never disabled. Rolling back therefore cannot cost any existing notification path.
